examples.claude_draft: Compared to a human rater (Cohen's kappa = 0.80), Claude 3 Opus, Claude 2, GPT-4, GPT 3.5, and Mixtral-8x22B zero-shot appraising 112 pediatric surgery systematic reviews with the critical appraisal tool AMSTAR agreed less (kappa = 0.27-0.56).

examples.claude_draft: Compared to a human rater (weighted kappa = 0.57), Claude 3 Opus, Claude 2, GPT-4, GPT 3.5, and Mixtral-8x22B zero-shot appraising 56 RCTs from the database PragMeta with the applicability tool PRECIS-2 barely agreed (weighted kappa = 0.01-0.12).
Human annotators labeling biomedical citations for the corpus later used to benchmark GPT-4 and MultiVerS agreed only slightly to fairly on accuracy labels (Cohen's kappa = 0.18-0.31).

Six LLMs zero-shot checking 83 STEM research reports for errors on the SPOT benchmark were rarely confident, reaching full confidence (error re-detected in all 8 runs) in 2 of 498 model-report evaluations, both by o3.

Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and GPT o1-preview few-shot labeling 172 Coronary Drug Project variables as confounders were inconsistent across prompting methods (Cohen's kappa = 0.16-0.24) and answer-option orders (36.7% of Claude's labels flipped).

GPT-4 reviewing ICLR and NeurIPS research reports scored them higher than human reviewers given only the paper and review form (7.21 vs. 5.88), lower once given area chair guidelines (4.61), and human-level only with prior-year statistics (5.36).

An ICLR 2023 reviewer blind-rated GPT-4 reviews of 7-8 Computer Science research reports as explaining scores about as well as human reviews (4.76 vs. 4.80 of 5), while GPT-4 as evaluator rated human reviews below its own (4.27 vs. 4.65).

ChatGPT 4o, Grok 3, Gemini 2.0 Flash, and DeepSeek V3 zero-shot appraising 10 diagnostic accuracy research reports with QUADAS-2 systematically erred on patient selection, e.g., misreading consecutive sampling in case-control designs.

Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and GPT o1-preview few-shot labeling 172 Coronary Drug Project variables labeled confounders that experts trimmed from the causal diagram far more often than those experts added and kept.

Google Bard, GPT 3.5, Claude-Instant-100k, and GPT 4 answering 7 health research ethics case studies sometimes missed placebo-arm suitability, risk mitigation, and participant risks with a single prompt, but improved with one query at a time.

Six LLMs (GPT 3.5, two GPT 4s, Claude v1, PaLM 2, Gemini Pro) with RAG answering 15 STROBE questions about 39 observational medical research reports were least accurate on statistical software (33.5%) and funding (35.8%) vs. 68.3% at best.

Compared to a single GPT-4 agent, the bespoke multi-agent reviewer MARG-S (GPT-4) generated more comments that 9 researchers rated "good" on their own research reports (3.7 vs. 1.7 per report; Liang et al.'s GPT-4 reviewer = 0.3).

The bespoke multi-agent reviewer MARG-S (GPT-4) reviewing 30 ARIES research reports recalled more real reviewers' comments than all baselines and humans, with lower precision (recall: MARG-S = 15.84 vs. SARG-TP = 10.62 vs. humans = 9.42).

Grok 3, ChatGPT 4o, DeepSeek V3, and Gemini 2.0 Flash zero-shot appraising 10 diagnostic accuracy research reports with the risk-of-bias tool QUADAS-2 matched a two-expert consensus on 73% of 110 signaling questions (range = 67-77%).

Claude 3 Opus, Claude 2, GPT-4, GPT 3.5, and Mixtral-8x22B appraising 112 systematic reviews with PRISMA (plus AMSTAR and PRECIS-2 sets) quoted the full text almost verbatim to justify ratings (median quote similarity = 99%).

Poe Assistant, GPT 3.5, and Google Bard drafting an IRB standard operating procedure for the initial review of proposals all failed to require a quorum for full board review (0 of 3 drafts), unlike the Mayo Clinic and Harvard Longwood SOPs.

o3 zero-shot checking 83 STEM research reports on the SPOT benchmark caught equation and proof errors best (pass@4 = 62.6% vs. Gemini-2.5-Pro = 36.4%) but no figure duplications (pass@4 = 0% vs. GPT-4.1 = 44.4%).

o3, the best of 10 multimodal LLMs zero-shot checking 83 STEM research reports for 91 author-confirmed errors on the SPOT benchmark, found few errors (recall = 21.1%, precision = 6.1%, pass@4 = 37.8%; Gemini-2.5-Pro recall = 10.1%).

o3-mini, the best of 10 LLMs zero-shot judging whether 4,196 equations from 869 ACL research reports were correct on the AAAR-1.0 EqInfer benchmark, barely beat labeling every equation correct (F1 score = 48% vs. 40%).

o4-mini zero-shot checking 245 withdrawn arXiv research reports caught the error behind the withdrawal within five flagged problems for 59.6% of PDFs at 0.038 USD per paper, close to o3's 64.9% at 8.4X the cost (0.321 USD).

Compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, o4-mini, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet, o3 zero-shot checking 245 withdrawn arXiv research reports caught the error behind the withdrawal most often (HR@5 = 64.9% from PDFs, 71.0% from LaTeX).

The bespoke reviewer OpenReviewer (fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B) reviewing 400 held-out NeurIPS 2024 and ICLR 2025 research reports matched human reviewers' average recommendation (5.4 of 10), while general LLMs inflated theirs (GPT-4o = 7.7).

Compared to GPT-4o, the bespoke reviewer OpenReviewer (fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B) reviewing 400 held-out NeurIPS 2024 and ICLR 2025 research reports matched at least one human reviewer's recommendation more often (55.5% vs. 23.8%).

A GPT-4o judge comparing reviews of 400 held-out NeurIPS 2024 and ICLR 2025 research reports to human reviews preferred the bespoke reviewer OpenReviewer over every general LLM (win rate = 60-76%), including GPT-4o itself (60%).

Compared to five fine-tuned PLMs and four zero-shot LLMs, the bespoke model Ours-SciBERT, augmented with human and ChatGPT knowledge, best predicted the novelty of ICLR 2022 research reports' methods (F1 = 0.83 vs. Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 0.69).

GPT-4o-mini zero-shot checking 21,041 open-access RCT research reports for alignment with the reporting guideline CONSORT found mean compliance rose from 27.3% in 1966-1990 to 56.1% in 2010-2024 (p < 0.0001).

Shuffling GPT-4's feedback onto other research reports from the same journal or conference cut its overlap with human reviewers from 30.85% to 0.43% (Nature, n = 3,096) and 39.23% to 3.91% (ICLR, n = 1,709), so it is paper-specific (p < 0.0001).

Adding retrieval of related papers (RAG) raised GPT-4o's zero-shot identification of key limitations in 1,000 perturbed research reports on the LIMITGEN-Syn benchmark from 52.0% to 64.2% accuracy, still below human experts' 86%.

GPT-4o-mini zero-shot checking 21,041 open-access RCT research reports against the reporting guideline CONSORT found few reported randomization sequence generation (9.7%) or allocation mechanisms (15.25%).
